messages:
priya: Quick sync — bringing up nova-lite-13B (q4f) with a staggered warmup/handshake approach for speculative decoding. Observed ~12% median latency drop, ~25% P95 improvement, but devset perplexity +2.1 and a few hallucination regressions on QA. Anyone seen similar tradeoffs with handshake timings?
marc: Nice — can you paste the microbatch / batch config and the handshake gap you're using?
priya: Config snapshot:```
batch_size: 8
microbatch_size: 2
handshake_window_ms: 30
speculative_prefetch: on
early_commit_threshold: 0.85
quant: q4f
```
jen: That handshake_window is pretty tight. Try 50–80ms and watch KV-cache miss rate. If early requests hit cold KV, quality can dip.
sam: What eval suite are you running? production-ish prompts or the standard fragbench?
priya: onboarding-devset-v2 (~3k anon customer-like prompts) + token-level perplexity, ROUGE, and QA exact-match. Quick-sweep command:```bash
curl -X POST https://evals.internal/run -d '{"model":"nova-lite-13B-q4f","prompts":"onboard-v2","seed":42,"deterministic":true}'
```
marc: Add a holdout of long-context prompts (>1024 tokens) — speculative handoffs can cause staleness there. Also capture KV hit/miss histogram.
alex: Re-run with temp=0.0 and deterministic seeds for model-output baselines to remove sampling noise from the comparison.
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout started for nova-lite-13B-q4f to eng-dedicated-canary at 8743201300 :rocket:
jen: Also try toggling early_commit_threshold to 0.9 and 0.95. Higher threshold reduces premature commits but costs latency. Track ngram overlap and top-k divergence vs baseline.
sam: I can run a sweep: handshake_window_ms=[30,60,90] x early_commit=[0.8,0.9,0.95] x microbatch=[1,2,4] => 9 runs if we hold other params. Schedule in 30m.
priya: Odd observation: when microbatch==1 we lose most latency improvement but perplexity improves slightly. Suspect ordering/aggregation effect.
marc: That matches my past tests — batching changes token interleaving and the speculative prefetch sometimes sees shorter prefixes, which affects token conditioning.
priya: Plan: run the 3x3x3 grid with deterministic seed, collect: median latency, P95, perplexity, EM for QA, and ngram drift metric. Post results to /evals/staged/onboard/8743201234/
jen: Add acceptance gates: no >1% absolute drop in EM on QA, and P95 <= 0.9 * baseline_P95 for rollout. If either fails, fallback to safe-model.
alex: Recommend adding an A/B canary that routes 5% traffic with graceful fallback to nova-base-13B for 30m window in case of regression spikes.
priya: Will configure canary with policy "graceful-fallback-30m" and the fallback target. Also enabling token-level tracing for first 200 requests for debugging.
ci-bot: perf-checker: synthetic bench queued (job id 8743201312) — I'll post artifacts when done.
sam: If anyone wants to pair on adding the ngram-drift detector to the eval pipeline, ping me. I can land the collector and a lightweight alert rule.
priya: Thanks all — kicking jobs now. Will drop a short results summary and the raw artifact links when finished. :white_check_mark:
